key_risks_to_thesis: JPM's 5Y EPS CAGR of +10% could re-accelerate if net interest income expands in a higher-for-longer rate environment, compressing the peer-relative P/E premium organically and validating the current valuation.

A significant market-share gain in investment banking or wealth management — visible in a revenue rebound above the $43.5B Q4 2025 peak in coming quarters — would invalidate the stalling-revenue argument and support multiple expansion.

If credit losses at peers (BAC, WFC, C) rise materially while JPM's superior risk management keeps provisions contained, JPM's premium P/E would be justified by relative earnings resilience, undermining the valuation-gap bear case.
